content.title: Site Disturbance Permit
content.summary: The City of Arvada requires a Site Disturbance Permit for any project disturbing 0.5 acres or more, effective January 1, 2025, following updates to the Municipal Code. Key changes include a lower disturbance threshold, mandatory Stormwater Management and erosion control plans, and updated permit fees. All applicants must be licensed, insured, and bonded as Municipal General Contractors with the city.
content.body:
All permits require the applicant to be licensed, insured, and bonded with the City of Arvada as a Municipal General Contractor.

The City of Arvada oversees construction sites within their jurisdiction to minimize the potential for pollutants to leave the site, including sediment. A Site Disturbance Permit is issued to owners, developers, contractors, or builders who must install and maintain adequate best management practices (BMPs) to control stormwater pollutants.

## 2024 Municipal Code Updates

The City has updated [Chapter 50 of Arvada's Municipal Code](https://library.municode.com/co/arvada/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTIICOOR_CH50DRSTQU) pertaining to drainage and stormwater quality. The code updates include modifications to the Site Disturbance Permit for development and construction. These changes will go into effect on **all Site Disturbance Permits applied for on or after January 1, 2025**.

Updates include:

1. Changing the required disturbance threshold from 10,000 square feet to 0.5 acres for Site Disturbance Permit coverage.
2. Requiring a Stormwater Management Plan, grading plan and erosion control plan for all projects that meet the permitting requirements.
3. Minor changes to the permit application and transfer forms.
4. Updates to the Site Disturbance Permit escrow which will require a cost estimate of temporary control measures to be submitted with the permit application.
5. Update to permit fees including the application fee, resubmittal fee, and the implementation of reinspection fees for non-compliant sites.
6. Application with the Colorado Department of Health and Environment (CDPHE) to be a Qualifying Local Program (QLP). This will mean that for small construction that are less than 5 acres of disturbed area, the project will not require CDPHE permitting and will only require a Site Disturbance Permit in an effort to streamline the permitting process.

These proposed code updates were approved by the Arvada City Council on August 19th, 2024 with an effective date of January 1, 2025 for Site Disturbance Permit requirements.

## Who needs a permit
**All projects that disturb 0.5 acres or more of land** must obtain an Arvada Site Disturbance Permit. Complete the Site Disturbance Permit Online Application and provide the required documentation for review.

**Projects that disturb 5 acres or more** must also obtain a [State Stormwater Discharges Associated With Construction Activity General Permit](https://cdphe.colorado.gov/cor400000-stormwater-discharge). The requirements of the State and City permits are similar. 

**The Site Disturbance Permit covers earthwork and grading activities ONLY**, in accordance with state and local stormwater requirements. All other construction activities related to public infrastructure, utilities, and structures must follow the appropriate [development](https://www.arvadaco.gov/651) and [building](https://www.arvadaco.gov/332) approval processes and permit applications.

## Contractor required

All permits will require the applicant to have a [Municipal General Contractor's License](https://www.arvadaco.gov/283) and be insured and bonded with the City of Arvada. Please contact the Engineering Division at 720-898-7640 with any questions.

## Site disturbance plan process

Sediment and erosion control plans that show how pollutants will be controlled must be submitted for review and approval and include the standard Plan Notes can be found in the [Mile High Flood District (MHFD) Criteria Manual, Volume 3](https://www.mhfd.org/criteria-manual-volume-3).

A narrative Stormwater Management Plan must be developed and submitted for review. The complexity of the plans submitted should be in accordance with the complexity of the proposed project. Please note:

- Approved sediment and erosion control plans must be followed, and updated as the site is developed.
- A grading plan is required.
- Disturbed earth is limited to 60 acres on any one site.
- Truck travel route map to and from the site is required.
	- Please complete this [Truck Route form](https://arvada-forms.app.transform.civicplus.com/forms/40913) and attach it to your permit.

### Small lots

An individual lot that is part of a larger common development must obtain a Site Disturbance Permit. If the lot is less than 0.5 acres, a permit will be awarded at no cost.

## Required documents

| Document | 0.5 acres or more | 5 acres or more |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Grading plan | Required | Required |
| Erosion Control Plan (BMPs) | Required | Required |
| Stormwater Management Plan (SWMP) | Required | Required |
| State construction permit |  | Required |
| Truck route map ([required form](https://arvada-forms.app.transform.civicplus.com/forms/40913)) | Required | Required |
| Dewatering permit (if applicable) | Case by case | Case by case |
| Cost estimate documents for BMPs only | Required | Required |

## Fees

Fees for the Site Development Permit vary from $400 to a maximum of $1050. A cash escrow or letter of credit in the amount provided as a cost estimate for temporary control measures must be on file with the City.

| Project disturbance area (acres) | Application fee | Resubmittal fee | Transfer fee |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.5 to 1 | $400 | $100 | $50 |
| 1 to 3 | $525 | $125 | $64 |
| 3 to 5 | $650 | $150 | $75 |
| 5 to 10 | $775 | $175 | $87.50 |
| 10 to 30 | $900 | $200 | $100 |
| 30 or more | $1050 | $250 | $125 |

**Reinspection fee** (based on 14 day compliance timeframe) for all projects is $150.
